skill.displayName: drivectl - your command-line tool for interacting with Google Drive

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only guide for using a Google Drive CLI; its requirements and instructions match the described purpose and do not request unrelated credentials or install arbitrary code.

dimensions.detail: The name/description match the SKILL.md content: it documents how to use the external drivectl CLI to interact with Drive, Docs, and Sheets. The only credential implied is the OAuth client_secret JSON used for Google auth, which is appropriate for this purpose. No unrelated binaries, env vars, or config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions stay within the declared purpose (listing, downloading, reading/updating Sheets/Docs). However, the documented drivectl call subcommand can invoke arbitrary Google API endpoints (including permission changes and other admin actions) when used — this is powerful but consistent with a generic Workspace CLI. The docs also direct use of local client_secret.json and outputting file contents to stdout, both expected but sensitive operations. Review commands before execution and limit OAuth scopes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only), so nothing is fetched or written by the skill itself. This reduces supply-chain risk but means the user/agent must already have a trusted drivectl binary on PATH; verify its provenance before use.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request environment variables or unrelated credentials. It expects a user-provided client_secret.json for OAuth and mentions cached tokens — both are normal for a CLI-based Google integration. No disproportionate access is requested by the SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill is user-invocable; it does not request persistent or system-wide privileges. Model invocation is allowed (platform default); combined with the CLI's broad API capability this could allow autonomous actions if the agent is permitted to run drivectl, so be mindful of agent autonomy settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is a documentation-only wrapper for an external drivectl CLI. Before using it: 1) ensure the drivectl binary on your system is from a trusted source (verify checksum or vendor) because the skill does not install or ship the binary; 2) protect your client_secret.json and cached OAuth tokens (store them securely and use least-privilege scopes); 3) be careful with the 'drivectl call' subcommand — it can call arbitrary Google APIs (including changing permissions), so review any generated commands before running; 4) remember that outputs (file contents) may be printed to stdout and could be forwarded by the agent, so avoid fetching sensitive files unless necessary and revoke tokens when finished. If you do not want the agent to autonomously execute drivectl, consider restricting the skill or disabling automated model invocation in your agent settings.
